docs.title: Voice AI Framework
docs.text: A modular, full-duplex conversational voice framework for Python 3.10+ Built for edge devices (Raspberry Pi, Linux) and laptops (macOS, Windows) powered by Google Gemini Live.

docs.title: 🌟 Overview
docs.text:
The Voice AI Framework is a developer-first library designed to build low-latency, full-duplex conversational voice assistants from scratch. It bridges physical hardware microphones and speakers with Google Gemini's real-time bidirectional streaming API (bidiGenerateContent), enabling natural spoken conversations with instant turn-taking and barge-in interruptions.

Unlike traditional voice wrappers that rely on sequential Speech-To-Text (STT) $\rightarrow$ LLM $\rightarrow$ Text-To-Speech (TTS) pipelines, this framework operates over a continuous, bidirectional audio WebSocket connection.

docs.title: ⚡ Ultra-Low Latency & Natural Barge-In
docs.text:
• Continuous 16kHz Streaming: Direct native hardware capture eliminates software resampling lag.
  • Natural Barge-In: When you speak while the assistant is speaking, the speaker buffer is cleared instantly (<50ms), allowing natural interruptions.
  • Acoustic Echo Resistance: Calibrated energy thresholds and streak detection prevent laptop speakers from interrupting themselves.

docs.title: 🧩 Self-Describing Tools with Prompt Templates
docs.text:
• Per-Tool Prompt Templates: Each tool declares its own usage rules, verbal etiquette, and confirmation protocols via prompt_instruction.
  • Dynamic Prompt Composition: When tools are registered into ToolRegistry, their prompt instructions are automatically composed into the effective system prompt sent during the Gemini Live handshake.

docs.title: 🎙️ Multi-Platform Audio Device Routing
docs.text:
• Independent Device Routing: Automatically detects and routes microphones and speakers across separate USB sound cards, I2S DACs, or built-in laptop hardware.
  • Cross-Platform: First-class support for macOS (CoreAudio), Windows (WASAPI/MME), Linux (ALSA/PulseAudio), and Raspberry Pi (snd-usb-audio).

docs.title: 🔍 Plug-and-Play RAG Vector Stores
docs.text:
• Semantic Retrieval: Built-in RAGRetriever orchestrates dense vector queries with fallback to keyword search.
  • Storage Backends: Works out-of-the-box with InMemoryVectorStore, QdrantVectorStore, and PineconeVectorStore.

docs.title: 📱 Safe WhatsApp Notifications
docs.text:
• Two-Turn Gate: Prevents accidental messages by requiring explicit verbal phone number verification before dispatching.
  • Multi-Gateway: Compatible with official Meta Cloud API and custom webhook endpoints.

docs.title: 🚀 Getting Started
docs.text:
Ready to build your first voice assistant in 5 minutes?

docs.title: 5-Minute Quickstart Guide
docs.text: This guide walks you through building and running your first production-ready, full-duplex conversational voice assistant from scratch using edgevoiceai.

docs.title: 1. Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python: >= 3.10 (Python 3.10, 3.11, or 3.12 recommended on Windows)
  • Google Gemini API Key: Get an API key from Google AI Studio
  • Microphone & Speaker: Built-in laptop audio, USB headset, or separate USB sound cards on Raspberry Pi.

docs.text:

docs.title: 4. Complete Runnable Code
docs.text:
Save the following code as assistant.py:

import asyncio
import os
from dotenv import load_dotenv

from edgevoiceai import (
    BaseTool,
    InMemoryMemoryStore,
    ToolExecutionContext,
    ToolRegistry,
    ToolResult,
    VoiceAgent,
    VoiceConfig,
)

# Load environment variables
load_dotenv()


# ── 1. Define a Custom Tool with its Own Prompt Template ─────────────────────
class BookAppointmentTool(BaseTool):
    """Schedules a customer consultation appointment."""

    @property
    def name(self) -> str:
        return "book_appointment"

    @property
    def description(self) -> str:
        return "Books a customer appointment for a requested service and date."

    @property
    def parameters_schema(self) -> dict:
        return {
            "type": "OBJECT",
            "properties": {
                "service": {
                    "type": "STRING",
                    "description": "The service type requested by the user.",
                },
                "date_time": {
                    "type": "STRING",
                    "description": "The requested date or time (e.g. 'tomorrow at 3 PM').",
                },
            },
            "required": ["service", "date_time"],
        }

    @property
    def prompt_instruction(self) -> str:
        """
        Self-describing prompt template.
        The framework automatically composes this into the AI's system prompt!
        """
        return (
            "• APPOINTMENT BOOKING PROTOCOL (`book_appointment`):\n"
            "  1. Only invoke this tool when the user explicitly requests to book a visit.\n"
            "  2. Verbally ask for their preferred day and service type before booking.\n"
            "  3. Confirm the appointment in 1 concise spoken sentence."
        )

    async def execute(self, args: dict, context: ToolExecutionContext) -> ToolResult:
        service = args.get("service", "Consultation")
        date_time = args.get("date_time", "soon")
        booking_id = "APT-992"

        print(f"\n📅 [Booking System] Confirmed: {service} for {date_time} (ID: {booking_id})")

        return ToolResult(
            status="confirmed",
            message=f"Appointment for {service} successfully scheduled for {date_time}. Booking ID is {booking_id}.",
            data={"booking_id": booking_id, "service": service, "date_time": date_time},
        )


# ── 2. Main Voice Application Runner ─────────────────────────────────────────
async def main() -> None:
    api_key = os.environ.get("GEMINI_API_KEY", "").strip()
    if not api_key:
        print("❌ Error: GEMINI_API_KEY environment variable is not set.")
        return

    # A. Register Tools
    tools = ToolRegistry()
    tools.register(BookAppointmentTool())

    # B. Configure Voice Agent
    config = VoiceConfig(
        api_key=api_key,
        model="gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview",  # Live bidirectional WebSocket model
        voice="Puck",                          # Voice name: Puck, Charon, Aoede, Fenrir, Kore
        system_instruction=(
            "You are Aria, an intelligent and courteous Voice AI assistant. "
            "Speak naturally, concisely (1-2 sentences), and warmly in English."
        ),
        # Hardware audio defaults (set None for system default mic & speaker)
        input_device=None,
        output_device=None,
    )

    # C. Instantiate Orchestrator
    agent = VoiceAgent(
        config=config,
        tools=tools,
        memory=InMemoryMemoryStore(),
    )

    # D. Register Event Callbacks
    agent.on_turn_complete = lambda text: print(f"\n🤖 [AI]: {text}")
    agent.on_interrupted = lambda: print("\n⚡ [User Interrupted AI]")
    agent.on_tool_executed = lambda name, args, res: print(f"🔧 [Tool Executed]: {name}")

    # Inspect the dynamically composed system prompt
    session_id = "user_quickstart_session"
    effective_prompt = await agent.build_effective_system_instruction(session_id)
    print("\n" + "=" * 60)
    print("📝 DYNAMICALLY COMPOSED SYSTEM PROMPT:")
    print("=" * 60)
    print(effective_prompt)
    print("=" * 60 + "\n")

    # E. Start Real-Time Voice Loop
    print("🎙️ Starting full-duplex voice loop. Speak into your microphone...")
    print("   (Press Ctrl+C to stop)")
    try:
        await agent.run_edge(session_id=session_id)
    except (KeyboardInterrupt, asyncio.CancelledError):
        print("\n👋 Stopping voice assistant...")
        agent.stop()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    try:
        asyncio.run(main())
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        pass

docs.title: Step A: Dynamic Prompt Composition
docs.text:
Notice that you did not have to hardcode tool guidelines into your persona prompt. When you implement: 

@property
def prompt_instruction(self) -> str:
    ...
ToolRegistry.build_tools_instruction() aggregates all active tool rules and VoiceAgent automatically injects them into the Gemini handshake. If you add or remove tools dynamically, the system prompt stays 100% in sync.

docs.title: Step B: Low-Latency Streaming & VAD
docs.text: VoiceAgent.run_edge() opens a native 16kHz microphone stream. The built-in VoiceActivityDetector monitors audio energy (RMS) and keeps syllable onsets intact so words like "Yes" or "Hey" are never clipped.

docs.title: Step C: Seamless Barge-In (Interruption)
docs.text: If the assistant is speaking through your speakers and you start talking, the framework detects your voice streak and clears the speaker queue in < 50 milliseconds, seamlessly yielding the turn back to you.

docs.title: Full-Duplex Streaming Architecture
docs.text:
Full-duplex voice communication means that both parties—the user and the AI agent—can speak and listen simultaneously. Unlike traditional half-duplex voice assistants that require rigid "push-to-talk" or wait for a turn to end before responding, the Voice AI Framework streams audio continuously over a single bidirectional WebSocket connection.

sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor User as User Microphone (16kHz PCM)
    participant Edge as VoiceAgent Edge Loop
    participant Gemini as Gemini Live API (bidiGenerateContent)
    actor Speaker as Audio Speaker (24kHz PCM)

    Note over User,Speaker: Full-Duplex Simultaneous I/O
    par Upstream Mic Stream
        User->>Edge: Capture 512 samples (32ms chunk)
        Edge->>Gemini: {"realtimeInput": {"mediaChunks": [{"data": "<base64>"}]}}
    and Downstream Audio Stream
        Gemini->>Edge: {"serverContent": {"modelTurn": {"parts": [{"inlineData": "<base64>"}]}}}
        Edge->>Speaker: Play 24kHz PCM chunk (non-blocking)
    end

    opt Barge-In Interruption
        User->>Edge: User speaks while AI is talking (RMS > Threshold)
        Edge->>Speaker: Clear audio queue instantly (stop playback)
        Edge->>Gemini: Send silence chunk & notify interruption
    end

docs.title: 1. Bidirectional WebSocket Connection
docs.text:
The framework communicates with Google's Gemini Multimodal Live API using the WebSocket endpoint:

wss://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/ws/google.ai.generativelanguage.v1beta.GenerativeService.BidiGenerateContent?key={API_KEY}

docs.title: Connection Handshake
docs.text:
Upon establishing the WebSocket connection, the agent sends an initial configuration payload specifying: 1. Model ID: models/gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview (or configured model). 2. Generation Configuration: Output audio modality, PCM encoding at 24kHz, and desired voice persona (e.g. Puck, Aoede, Charon). 3. System Instructions: The composed dynamic prompt containing persona rules, memory state, and tool schemas. 4. Function Declarations: OpenAPI-compatible schemas for all registered tools.

setup_payload = {
    "setup": {
        "model": "models/gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview",
        "generationConfig": {
            "responseModalities": ["AUDIO"],
            "speechConfig": {
                "voiceConfig": {
                    "prebuiltVoiceConfig": {
                        "voiceName": "Puck"
                    }
                }
            }
        },
        "systemInstruction": {
            "parts": [{"text": effective_prompt}]
        },
        "tools": tool_declarations
    }
}

docs.title: 2. Audio Framing & Specifications
docs.text:
Audio data is streamed in raw Linear PCM format without compression overhead, minimizing processing and encoding latencies:

Parameter Input Stream (Microphone) Output Stream (Speaker) Sample Rate 16,000 Hz (16 kHz) 24,000 Hz (24 kHz) Channels 1 (Mono) 1 (Mono) Bit Depth 16-bit signed integer (int16, little-endian) 16-bit signed integer (int16, little-endian) Chunk Size 512 samples (1,024 bytes) Variable streaming packets Chunk Duration 32.0 milliseconds Continuous stream

docs.title: 3. Concurrent Worker Coroutines
docs.text:
Inside VoiceAgent.run_edge, audio I/O and protocol management are split into two parallel asynchronous tasks:

flowchart LR
    subgraph MicLoop ["Microphone Loop (_capture_and_send)"]
        A["MicrophoneStream"] --> B["VAD & Noise Gate"]
        B --> C["Interrupt Streak Detection"]
        C --> D["WebSocket Send realtimeInput"]
    end

    subgraph SpkLoop ["Speaker Loop (_receive_and_play)"]
        E["WebSocket Recv"] --> F{"Message Type"}
        F -->|inlineData Audio| G["AudioPlayer Queue"]
        F -->|toolCall| H["Execute Tool & Send toolResponse"]
        F -->|outputTranscription| I["Emit Realtime Transcript"]
    end

docs.title: Upstream: _capture_and_send
docs.text:
• Reads 512-sample PCM chunks non-blockingly from MicrophoneStream.
  • Calculates Root Mean Square (RMS) energy to detect speech vs. background noise.
  • Checks if the user is interrupting active AI playback (barge-in).
  • Encodes speech chunks to Base64 and sends them over the WebSocket connection.

docs.title: Downstream: _receive_and_play
docs.text:
• Listens for incoming server frames from Gemini.
  • Decodes Base64 audio PCM and feeds it into the low-latency AudioPlayer thread queue.
  • Extracts real-time spoken transcripts (serverContent.outputTranscription.text) for event listeners and UI display.
  • Intercepts toolCall invocations, executes the requested function asynchronously, and returns the toolResponse in the same duplex session.

docs.title: 4. Latency Optimization Techniques
docs.text: To achieve sub-second conversational latency: 1. Native 16kHz Negotiation: Captures directly at 16kHz hardware rate if supported by the sound card, bypassing CPU-heavy resampling filters (audioop.ratecv). 2. Compact 512-Frame Buffers: Cuts frame buffering delay to 32ms compared to traditional 1024 or 2048 buffers. 3. Calibrated Trailing Hang Frames: Emits ~480ms of trailing room ambient sound after user speech ends. This allows Gemini's server-side neural VAD to immediately identify sentence completion and begin token generation without timeout delays. 4. WebSocket Ping Interval: Set to ping_interval=None to avoid interfering with Gemini Live's proprietary streaming protocol.

docs.title: Dynamic Prompt Composition
docs.text:
In high-performance voice AI systems, a static system prompt often fails: - It bloats the context window with instructions for tools that aren't enabled. - It cannot easily inject dynamic caller identity or user profile data. - It struggles to enforce strict conversational guardrails (such as 2-turn verbal verification protocols).

The EdgeVoiceAI Framework solves this with Three-Layer Dynamic Prompt Composition, managed automatically by VoiceAgent.build_effective_system_instruction.

flowchart TD
    subgraph L1 ["Layer 1: Base Persona"]
        A["Voice Persona & Identity"]
        B["Spoken Output Brevity Rules"]
    end

    subgraph L2 ["Layer 2: Memory & Context"]
        C["User Profile: Name, Phone, Role"]
        D["Recent Dialogue Memory"]
    end

    subgraph L3 ["Layer 3: Active Tool Rules"]
        E["Tool A: Booking Rules"]
        F["Tool B: WhatsApp 2-Turn Protocol"]
        G["Tool C: Weather JIT Rules"]
    end

    L1 --> H["VoiceAgent Prompt Builder"]
    L2 --> H
    L3 --> H

    H --> I["Effective Gemini System Instruction"]

docs.title: 1. The Three Layers of Voice Prompts
Layer 1: Base Persona & Spoken Conversational Rules
docs.text:
Defines who the agent is and how it speaks. Spoken language must be radically more concise than written chatbots:

You are a warm, helpful, and concise voice AI assistant.
Speak in natural, conversational sentences suitable for speech synthesis.
Keep spoken responses to 1-2 brief sentences unless explaining detailed steps.
Never output markdown tables, asterisks, or bullet lists; speak naturally.

docs.title: Layer 2: Memory & Caller Context
docs.text:
Dynamically injects caller information retrieved from session storage or SQLite databases:

[CURRENT CALLER CONTEXT]
• User ID: user_492
• Name: Ramesh Patel
• Preferred Language: English / Gujarati
• Location: Anand, Gujarat

docs.title: Layer 3: Active Tool Rules & Guardrails
docs.text:
Each tool subclassing BaseTool can override prompt_instruction to inject instructions that govern how and when the tool may be invoked:

class SendWhatsAppMessageTool(BaseTool):
    # ...
    @property
    def prompt_instruction(self) -> str | None:
        return (
            "• NOTIFICATION & MESSAGING PROTOCOL (`send_whatsapp_message`):\n"
            "  1. When the user asks to send an answer or provides their phone number, "
            "DO NOT call `send_whatsapp_message` in that turn.\n"
            "  2. First say verbally: 'Your phone number is [phone_number], correct?' and stop speaking.\n"
            "  3. Only in the subsequent turn, after the user confirms (e.g. 'yes/correct'), call `send_whatsapp_message`.\n"
            "  4. Never invent or use dummy phone numbers like '0000000000'."
        )

docs.title: 2. Dynamic Assembly in VoiceAgent
docs.text:
The agent combines these layers into a unified prompt string whenever the voice agent initializes or reconnects:

# Inside VoiceAgent:
sys_instruction = await agent.build_effective_system_instruction(session_id="default")

Under the hood: 1. Starts with config.system_instruction. 2. Asynchronously fetches caller profile data from memory.build_context_prompt(session_id). 3. Calls tools.build_tools_instruction(), which loops through all registered BaseTool instances, collecting every non-empty tool.prompt_instruction.

docs.title: 3. Benefits of Dynamic Composition
docs.text:
1. Zero Hallucination of Parameters: By explicitly instructing the model to verbally confirm missing or sensitive parameters, tools are never called with invented arguments (such as fake phone numbers or default appointment times).
  2. Context Efficiency: If a tool is removed from the registry, its prompt template is omitted automatically, saving prompt tokens and keeping the model focused.
  3. Multi-Agent & Multi-Tenant Support: Agents serving different caller roles (e.g. customer vs. administrator) dynamically receive different tool subsets and tailored instructions.

docs.title: Voice Activity Detection (VAD) & Barge-In
docs.text: Natural human conversation requires seamless interruptions (barge-in) and accurate speech boundary detection. The framework implements an edge-optimized Voice Activity Detection (VAD) pipeline combined with immediate playback queue interruption.

docs.title: 1. How VAD Works on the Edge
docs.text:
Speech detection happens in real-time inside MicrophoneStream and VoiceAgent._capture_and_send using Root Mean Square (RMS) energy calculation on 16-bit PCM audio.

flowchart TD
    A[Raw 512-sample PCM chunk] --> B[Compute RMS Energy]
    B --> C{Is AI Speaking?}

    C -->|No: User Speech Gate| D{RMS > noise_gate_threshold?}
    D -->|Yes| E[State: SPEAKING]
    D -->|No| F{Was recently speaking?}
    F -->|Yes: within hang_frames| G[State: HANG_FRAMES]
    F -->|No: silence| H[Drop chunk / Keep Pre-Buffer]

    C -->|Yes: Barge-In Gate| I{RMS > ai_interrupt_threshold?}
    I -->|Yes| J[Increment Interrupt Streak Counter]
    I -->|No| K[Reset Interrupt Streak Counter]

    J --> L{Streak >= streak_trigger?}
    L -->|Yes| M[TRIGGER BARGE-IN: Flush AudioPlayer Queue]
    L -->|No| N[Ignore transient noise spike]

docs.title: RMS Energy Calculation
docs.text:
The RMS value represents the sound volume of an audio frame:

$$\text{RMS} = \sqrt{\frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^{N} x_i^2}$$

In Python (audioop or native struct unpack):

import audioop

rms = audioop.rms(raw_pcm_chunk, 2)  # 2 bytes per sample for 16-bit PCM

docs.title: 2. Speech Boundary Detection
docs.text: To avoid cutting off the beginning of words (consonant onsets) or chopping off the ends of sentences, the framework uses a two-stage sliding window:

docs.title: 1. Pre-buffering (pre_buffer_max_frames=8)
docs.text: Human speech typically begins with soft consonants (e.g. "p", "t", "s") whose amplitude is lower than the active speech threshold. - The stream maintains a circular buffer of the last 8 frames (~256 ms). - When the RMS threshold is exceeded, the pre-buffered frames are immediately flushed to the upstream stream. - This ensures zero loss of initial syllables.

docs.title: 2. Hang Frames (hang_frames=15)
docs.text: Natural speech contains brief pauses between words or clauses: - When RMS drops below noise_gate_threshold, the stream does not cut off immediately. - It continues sending for 15 frames (~480 ms) of ambient room noise. - This prevents speech fragmentation and gives Gemini's neural VAD the natural acoustic cue needed to recognize turn completion.

docs.title: 3. Barge-In Interruption Detection
docs.text:
When the AI is speaking, sound waves travel from the laptop/device speakers into the surrounding room and can bleed into the microphone.

To prevent the AI from interrupting itself due to speaker bleed while still allowing the human user to interrupt:

docs.title: The Dual-Threshold Strategy
docs.text: State Active Threshold Default RMS Purpose AI is Silent noise_gate_threshold 250 Detects soft human speech onset while ignoring room hum. AI is Speaking ai_interrupt_threshold 2800 Requires loud intentional speech above speaker echo bleed.

docs.title: Streak Detection (streak_trigger=4)
docs.text: A momentary click, cough, or acoustic echo spike lasts for 1–2 frames (30–60 ms). To avoid false barge-ins: - The system requires 4 consecutive frames (~128 ms) exceeding ai_interrupt_threshold before triggering an interruption. - Once triggered: 1. audio_player.clear() immediately purges buffered audio chunks from the speaker queue. 2. The speaker becomes instantly silent. 3. The on_interrupted callback is dispatched. 4. The user's new utterance is streamed directly to Gemini to take over the conversation turn.

docs.title: 4. Hardware Calibration Guide
docs.text:
Different audio environments require different sensitivity profiles:

from edgevoiceai import AudioConfig

# Setup for quiet office with USB Headset
headset_config = AudioConfig(
    noise_gate_threshold=150,     # Very sensitive mic close to mouth
    ai_interrupt_threshold=1200,   # Low echo bleed through headphones
    hang_frames=12,
    streak_trigger=3
)

# Setup for laptop built-in mic & built-in speakers (High speaker bleed)
laptop_config = AudioConfig(
    noise_gate_threshold=300,
    ai_interrupt_threshold=2800,   # High threshold to resist loud speaker echo
    hang_frames=15,
    streak_trigger=4
)

# Setup for noisy kiosk or agricultural field unit
field_config = AudioConfig(
    noise_gate_threshold=600,     # Filter out wind / tractor rumble
    ai_interrupt_threshold=3500,
    hang_frames=18,
    streak_trigger=5
)

docs.title: Custom Tools & Prompt Templates
docs.text:
Tools are what give a Voice AI assistant real-world agency—querying databases, scheduling calendar visits, triggering notifications, or checking telemetry sensors.

In voice applications, tool execution is fundamentally different from text chatbots: - Verbal Etiquette: The AI must not recite raw JSON, database IDs, or technical error messages aloud. - Natural Confirmation: Destructive or outbound actions (like sending messages or booking slots) require verbal confirmation before execution. - Conversational Brevity: Responses must be synthesized into 1–2 spoken sentences.

edgevoiceai introduces Self-Describing Tools with Prompt Templates to solve these challenges modularly.

docs.title: 1. The BaseTool Specification
docs.text:
Every tool in edgevoiceai subclasses BaseTool:

from typing import Any, Dict, Optional
from edgevoiceai import BaseTool, ToolExecutionContext, ToolResult

class MyCustomTool(BaseTool):
    @property
    def name(self) -> str:
        """Unique identifier used by Gemini Live for function calling."""
        return "my_tool"

    @property
    def description(self) -> str:
        """Detailed description informing Gemini when and why to call this tool."""
        return "Fetches real-time status updates for a user account."

    @property
    def parameters_schema(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """JSON Schema defining the expected arguments."""
        return {
            "type": "OBJECT",
            "properties": {
                "account_id": {"type": "STRING", "description": "The customer account ID."}
            },
            "required": ["account_id"],
        }

    @property
    def prompt_instruction(self) -> Optional[str]:
        """Usage rules and verbal guidelines injected into the effective system prompt."""
        return (
            "• ACCOUNT STATUS RULE (`my_tool`):\n"
            "  1. Only invoke this tool when the user asks for account status.\n"
            "  2. Report the balance in 1 spoken sentence without reading internal ledger codes."
        )

    async def execute(self, args: Dict[str, Any], context: ToolExecutionContext) -> ToolResult:
        """Asynchronous execution logic."""
        account_id = args.get("account_id", "")
        # ... fetch data ...
        return ToolResult(
            status="success",
            message="Account is active with a balance of $120.",
            data={"balance": 120.0, "status": "active"},
        )

docs.title: The Problem with Monolithic Prompts
docs.text: In traditional voice agents, developers write massive, 200-line system prompts containing usage rules for every single tool. When you add, remove, or modify a tool, you have to carefully edit the monolithic prompt, leading to prompt drift and hallucinations.

docs.title: The Solution: Self-Describing Tools
docs.text:
In edgevoiceai, every tool defines its own @property prompt_instruction.

When tools are registered in the ToolRegistry: 

tools = ToolRegistry()
tools.register(AppointmentTool())
tools.register(WhatsAppNotificationTool(config=whatsapp_config))
tools.register(KnowledgeBaseTool(...))

The framework automatically compiles all active instructions into a clean prompt section:

[ACTIVE TOOLS & USAGE RULES]
• APPOINTMENT BOOKING PROTOCOL (`book_appointment`):
  1. Only invoke this tool when the user explicitly requests to book a visit.
  2. Verbally ask for their preferred day and service type before booking.
  3. Confirm the appointment in 1 concise spoken sentence.

• NOTIFICATION & MESSAGING PROTOCOL (`send_whatsapp_message`):
  1. When the user asks to send an answer or provides their phone number, DO NOT call `send_whatsapp_message` in that turn.
  2. First say verbally: 'Your phone number is [phone_number], correct?' and stop speaking.
  3. Only in the subsequent turn, after the user confirms (e.g. 'yes/correct'), call `send_whatsapp_message`.
  4. Never invent or use dummy phone numbers like '0000000000'.

When VoiceAgent.build_effective_system_instruction() runs, it combines: 1. Base Persona Prompt (identity & voice tone) 2. User Memory / Profile Context (known user facts) 3. Active Tool Rules (aggregated dynamically via tools.build_tools_instruction())

docs.title: 3. The Strict 2-Turn Confirmation Pattern
docs.text:
Outbound notifications (SMS, WhatsApp, emails) or financial actions should never be triggered on the first turn. If a user says "Send that to my WhatsApp at 9876543210", the model might mishear a digit or dispatch prematurely.

edgevoiceai includes a built-in TwoTurnConfirmationNotificationTool that enforces a verbal confirmation gate:

sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor User as User (Voice)
    participant Agent as VoiceAgent (AI)
    participant Tool as TwoTurnConfirmationTool

    User->>Agent: "Send the summary to 9876543210 on WhatsApp"
    Note over Agent: Turn 1: Gate Closed
    Agent->>User: "Your phone number is 9876543210, right?"
    User->>Agent: "Yes, that's correct."
    Note over Agent: Turn 2: Gate Verified
    Agent->>Tool: execute(phone="9876543210", message="...")
    Tool-->>Agent: ToolResult(status="sent")
    Agent->>User: "I have dispatched the details to your WhatsApp!"

To create your own 2-turn confirmation tool, inherit from TwoTurnConfirmationNotificationTool:

from edgevoiceai import TwoTurnConfirmationNotificationTool, ToolExecutionContext, ToolResult

class SecureOrderCancellationTool(TwoTurnConfirmationNotificationTool):
    @property
    def name(self) -> str:
        return "cancel_customer_order"

    @property
    def description(self) -> str:
        return "Cancels a customer order after explicit verbal 2-turn confirmation."

    async def _send_notification(self, target: str, content: str) -> None:
        # target is the verified Order ID
        await order_db.cancel_order(order_id=target, reason=content)

docs.title: 4. Understanding ToolResult
docs.text:
The return value of execute() is a ToolResult dataclass:

@dataclass
class ToolResult:
    status: str                         # "success", "error", "pending_confirmation", etc.
    message: Optional[str] = None       # Concise text feedback for Gemini's next turn
    data: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None  # Structured data payload
    jit_instruction: Optional[str] = None # Just-In-Time instruction for the model
    client_event: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None # Optional event pushed to UI clients
    queued_audio_url: Optional[str] = None # Audio file to play immediately after AI speech

docs.title: Just-In-Time (JIT) Instructions
docs.text:
A JIT instruction gives dynamic, context-specific guidance to Gemini for that specific turn only:

return ToolResult(
    status="success",
    message="Sensor temperature is 42 degrees Celsius.",
    jit_instruction=(
        "Warn the user immediately that the machine temperature is critical. "
        "Recommend shutting down the motor in 1 spoken sentence."
    )
)

Gemini receives this instruction in the functionResponse payload and immediately acts on it without cluttering the global system prompt.

docs.title: 5. Complete Example: Weather & Environmental Sensor Tool
docs.text:
Here is a complete, copy-pasteable example of a custom hardware telemetry tool:

import asyncio
from typing import Any, Dict
from edgevoiceai import BaseTool, ToolExecutionContext, ToolResult, ToolRegistry

class WarehouseSensorTool(BaseTool):
    """Monitors live warehouse humidity and temperature sensors."""

    @property
    def name(self) -> str:
        return "read_warehouse_sensors"

    @property
    def description(self) -> str:
        return "Reads current temperature and humidity telemetry from warehouse sensors."

    @property
    def parameters_schema(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "type": "OBJECT",
            "properties": {
                "zone": {
                    "type": "STRING",
                    "description": "Warehouse zone name (e.g. 'cold_storage', 'loading_dock').",
                }
            },
            "required": ["zone"],
        }

    @property
    def prompt_instruction(self) -> str:
        return (
            "• WAREHOUSE SENSOR RULE (`read_warehouse_sensors`):\n"
            "  1. When the user asks about temperature or warehouse conditions, call this tool.\n"
            "  2. Report both temperature and humidity in a conversational tone.\n"
            "  3. Do not invent readings without calling the tool."
        )

    async def execute(self, args: Dict[str, Any], context: ToolExecutionContext) -> ToolResult:
        zone = args.get("zone", "cold_storage")

        # Simulate hardware sensor read
        temp_c = 4.2 if zone == "cold_storage" else 22.5
        humidity = 85.0 if zone == "cold_storage" else 45.0

        return ToolResult(
            status="success",
            message=f"Zone '{zone}' reading: {temp_c}°C, {humidity}% humidity.",
            data={"zone": zone, "temp_c": temp_c, "humidity": humidity},
            jit_instruction=(
                f"State the {zone} conditions clearly in 1 spoken sentence. "
                "Confirm that temperature is within optimal range."
            ),
        )


# Registering into the Registry:
tools = ToolRegistry()
tools.register(WarehouseSensorTool())

docs.title: Hardware Audio & Edge Device Routing
docs.text:
edgevoiceai is built from the ground up for edge hardware (Raspberry Pi, mini PCs, robotics) as well as development laptops (macOS, Linux, Windows).

One of its most powerful capabilities is Independent Device Routing: you can route audio input to one physical device (e.g. an omnidirectional USB microphone array) and audio output to a completely different physical device (e.g. an I2S DAC, 3.5mm speaker, or Bluetooth headset).

docs.title: 1. Inspecting Connected Audio Devices
docs.text:
To list all physical audio input and output devices connected to your system:

from edgevoiceai import AudioDeviceManager

devices = AudioDeviceManager.list_devices()
for d in devices:
    kind = "🎙️ INPUT" if d.max_input_channels > 0 else "🔊 OUTPUT"
    print(f"[{d.index}] {kind}: {d.name} (Rate: {d.default_sample_rate}Hz)")

docs.title: 2. Configuring Audio Routing in VoiceConfig
docs.text:
You can configure hardware devices using either: - Device Index (int): Exact hardware index from list_devices(). - Device Name Substring (str): Case-insensitive fuzzy matching (e.g. "USB PnP", "Built-in", "JBL", "AirPods", "hw:1,0"). - None: Uses system default audio input/output.

from edgevoiceai import VoiceConfig

config = VoiceConfig(
    api_key="...",
    # Route input to external USB microphone by name substring
    input_device="USB PnP Audio Device",
    # Route output to external speakers by index or name
    output_device="Built-in Output",
    # Native 16kHz direct capture
    mic_capture_rate=16000,
    speaker_sample_rate=24000,
)

docs.title: 3. Platform-Specific Setup Guides
docs.text: macOS (Apple Silicon & Intel)Raspberry Pi & Linux (Edge Devices)Windows 10 & 11

docs.title: CoreAudio & Microphone Permissions
docs.text:
1. Microphone Access: Grant Terminal, VS Code, or your IDE microphone access under System Settings → Privacy & Security → Microphone.
  2. Lazy Audio Device Initialization: On macOS, opening both PyAudio and Pygame's SDL audio mixer at the exact same instant can cause a low-level CoreAudio mutex lock. The framework automatically initializes MediaAudioPlayer lazily on playback to keep signal delivery and Ctrl+C handling responsive.
  3. Device Names: Use substring matches like "MacBook Air Microphone", "AirPods", or "BlackHole".

docs.title: System Prerequisites
docs.text:
Install PortAudio and ALSA development libraries: 

sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y portaudio19-dev libasound2-dev python3-pyaudio alsa-utils

docs.title: Checking ALSA Device Cards
docs.text:
arecord -l   # Lists capture cards (e.g. card 1: USB PnP Sound Device)
aplay -l     # Lists playback cards (e.g. card 0: bcm2835 Headphones, or I2S DAC)

docs.title: Automatic PortAudio Negotiation
docs.text:
Many cheap USB microphones on Raspberry Pi reject 16,000 Hz if opened directly in native mode because their internal DSP only supports 44,100 Hz or 48,000 Hz.

MicrophoneStream automatically performs Hardware Sample Rate Negotiation: 1. Tests native 16000 Hz capture (fastest, zero CPU overhead). 2. If the USB soundcard rejects 16kHz, it falls back to 48000 Hz or 44100 Hz and resamples automatically using audioop.ratecv.

docs.title: Autostart on Boot (Systemd Service)
docs.text:
Create /etc/systemd/system/voice-agent.service: 

[Unit]
Description=Voice AI Assistant Edge Service
After=network-online.target sound.target

[Service]
Type=simple
User=pi
WorkingDirectory=/home/pi/voice-ai
ExecStart=/home/pi/voice-ai/venv/bin/python main.py
Restart=always
RestartSec=5

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
Enable and start the service: 
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable voice-agent.service
sudo systemctl start voice-agent.service

docs.title: WASAPI & MME Audio Drivers
docs.text:
1. Microphone Privacy: Enable microphone permissions in Settings → Privacy & Security → Microphone.
  2. Device Naming: Windows devices often appear with driver suffixes like "Microphone (Realtek High Definition Audio)" or "Headset Earphone (USB Audio Device)".
  3. Substrings: Pass "Realtek" or "USB Audio" directly to input_device and output_device.

docs.title: Windows Python Versions & PyAudio
docs.text:
• Recommended Python: Use Python 3.10, 3.11, or 3.12. These versions have official pre-compiled wheels for PyAudio and require no external compilers.
  • Resolving Microsoft Visual C++ 14.0 or greater is required: This occurs on Windows if running Python 3.14+ (which currently lacks pre-built wheels on PyPI) or if pip attempts a source build. To resolve:
  • Create your environment with Python 3.11 or 3.12: 
    py -3.11 -m venv venv
.\venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
pip install edgevoiceai
  • Or install Microsoft Visual C++ Build Tools and select "Desktop development with C++".

docs.title: 4. Latency & Buffer Calibration
docs.text: Parameter Default Recommended Value Impact mic_capture_rate 16000 16000 Native capture eliminates software resampling latency. speaker_sample_rate 24000 24000 Matches Gemini Live native 24kHz PCM output. frames_per_buffer 512 512 32ms capture packets / 21ms playback chunks. noise_gate_threshold 250 250 (indoor) / 1200+ (noisy/outdoor) RMS audio energy required to open microphone. ai_interrupt_threshold 2800 2800 (speakers) / 1800 (headphones) Prevents acoustic loopback while allowing barge-in. hang_frames 15 12-18 (~380-570ms) Ambient audio frames sent after speech ends for turn detection.

docs.title: Memory & Context Profiles
docs.text:
Full-duplex conversational voice agents often interact with users across multiple turns or multiple days. Remembering user facts (e.g. name, location, preferred language, membership tier) makes the assistant feel intelligent and personal.

edgevoiceai separates memory into: 1. Dialogue History: Raw chronological turns (ChatMessage models). 2. Entity & Profile State: Key-value facts extracted during conversations. 3. Dynamic Prompt Injection: Automatically formatting profile context into the system prompt.

docs.title: 1. Memory Store Implementations
docs.text:
edgevoiceai provides two standard implementations:

  • InMemoryMemoryStore: Ephemeral, zero-dependency in-memory dictionary. Ideal for testing and single-session interactions.
  • SQLiteMemoryStore: Lightweight file-backed SQL database. Persists conversations and user profiles across application restarts with async queries.

docs.title: 2. Using InMemoryMemoryStore
docs.text:
import asyncio
from edgevoiceai import InMemoryMemoryStore

async def example():
    memory = InMemoryMemoryStore()
    session_id = "user_42"

    # Pre-seed known profile details
    await memory.update_profile(session_id, {
        "user_name": "Rohan Sharma",
        "city": "Mumbai",
        "tier": "Premium Gold",
    })

    # Add dialogue turns
    await memory.add_message(session_id, role="user", content="Hello!")
    await memory.add_message(session_id, role="assistant", content="Hello Rohan! How can I help you today?")

    # Inspect the dynamically generated context prompt
    context_prompt = await memory.build_context_prompt(session_id)
    print(context_prompt)

asyncio.run(example())

Output: 

[KNOWN USER CONTEXT & PROFILE]
• user_name: Rohan Sharma
• city: Mumbai
• tier: Premium Gold

docs.title: 3. Persistent Memory with SQLiteMemoryStore
docs.text:
For production edge devices or servers, use SQLiteMemoryStore:

from edgevoiceai import SQLiteMemoryStore

memory = SQLiteMemoryStore(db_path="conversations.db")

The database automatically initializes the required conversations, messages, and user_profiles tables.

docs.title: 4. Automatic Context Injection in VoiceAgent
docs.text:
When you pass a memory store to VoiceAgent:

agent = VoiceAgent(
    config=config,
    tools=tools,
    memory=memory,
)

At the start of every session or turn, agent.build_effective_system_instruction(session_id) automatically calls memory.build_context_prompt(session_id) and injects the facts directly into Gemini's system instructions.

docs.title: RAG & Vector Database Stores
docs.text:
Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) allows your Voice AI assistant to query authoritative knowledge bases, documentation, policies, and farmer experiences without hallucinating facts.

edgevoiceai provides a unified RAG abstraction with plug-and-play vector databases and built-in offline fallbacks.

docs.title: 1. Core Architecture
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    UserQuery["User Voice Query\n('How to prune apple trees?')"] --> Embeddings["GeminiEmbeddings\n(768-dim dense vectors)"]
    Embeddings --> Retriever["RAGRetriever"]
    Retriever --> PrimaryStore["Primary Vector Store\n(Pinecone / Qdrant)"]
    PrimaryStore -.->|Offline / No Matches| FallbackStore["Fallback Store\n(InMemory Vector Store + BM25 Keyword)"]
    Retriever --> KBTool["KnowledgeBaseTool\n(Synthesizes Context + JIT Instruction)"]
    KBTool --> GeminiLive["Gemini Live Response\n(1-2 Concise Spoken Sentences)"]

docs.title: 2. Choosing a Vector Store
docs.text:
edgevoiceai provides 3 standard vector store implementations:

Vector Store Class Persistence Ideal For In-Memory InMemoryVectorStore Memory (ephemeral) / Local Dict Zero-dependency testing, offline edge devices, small knowledge bases (<10k chunks). Qdrant QdrantVectorStore On-premise Docker / Qdrant Cloud Private server hosting, high-throughput self-hosted deployments. Pinecone PineconeVectorStore Managed Cloud Serverless Fully managed cloud production environments.

docs.title: 3. Quick Example: In-Memory Semantic Search
docs.text:
import asyncio
from edgevoiceai import (
    DocumentChunk,
    GeminiEmbeddings,
    InMemoryVectorStore,
    KnowledgeBaseTool,
    RAGRetriever,
)

async def setup_rag(api_key: str) -> KnowledgeBaseTool:
    # 1. Initialize embeddings generator
    embeddings = GeminiEmbeddings(api_key=api_key)

    # 2. Initialize vector store
    store = InMemoryVectorStore()

    # 3. Seed knowledge documents
    docs = [
        DocumentChunk(
            id="doc_1",
            title="Return Policy",
            text="Customers can return unopened products within 30 days for a full refund.",
        ),
        DocumentChunk(
            id="doc_2",
            title="Support Hours",
            text="Live support is available Monday to Friday from 9 AM to 6 PM EST.",
        ),
    ]

    # Generate vectors and upsert
    vectors = await embeddings.embed_texts([d.text for d in docs])
    await store.upsert(docs, vectors)

    # 4. Wrap with RAGRetriever
    retriever = RAGRetriever(
        embedding_model=embeddings,
        vector_store=store,
        default_limit=2,
    )

    # 5. Create KnowledgeBaseTool
    return KnowledgeBaseTool(
        name="search_company_knowledge",
        description="Searches company documentation, return policies, and support hours.",
        parameters_schema={
            "type": "OBJECT",
            "properties": {
                "query": {"type": "STRING", "description": "The search question or topic."}
            },
            "required": ["query"],
        },
        retriever_func=retriever.retrieve,
        prompt_instruction=(
            "• KNOWLEDGE RETRIEVAL RULE (`search_company_knowledge`):\n"
            "  1. When the user asks about return policies or hours, call this tool.\n"
            "  2. Base your response strictly on the retrieved knowledge in 1-2 spoken sentences.\n"
            "  3. Do not invent company policies."
        ),
    )

docs.title: Qdrant Vector Store
docs.text:
from edgevoiceai import QdrantVectorStore

store = QdrantVectorStore(
    host="localhost",
    port=6333,
    collection_name="company_knowledge",
)

docs.title: Pinecone Vector Store
docs.text:
from edgevoiceai import PineconeVectorStore

store = PineconeVectorStore(
    api_key="your-pinecone-api-key",
    index_name="company-knowledge",
)

docs.title: 5. Offline Fallback & Keyword Search
docs.text:
If your primary cloud vector database (Qdrant/Pinecone) is unreachable or yields no matching results, RAGRetriever can automatically query an in-memory fallback store and run keyword matching:

retriever = RAGRetriever(
    embedding_model=embeddings,
    vector_store=cloud_store,
    fallback_store=in_memory_store,
)

docs.title: 6. Integrating RAG with VoiceAgent
docs.text:
Once your RAGRetriever is configured, attach it to a BaseTool (or KnowledgeBaseTool) and register it with your VoiceAgent:

import os
from edgevoiceai import (
    BaseTool,
    ToolExecutionContext,
    ToolResult,
    VoiceAgent,
    VoiceConfig,
)

class KnowledgeTool(BaseTool):
    @property
    def name(self) -> str:
        return "search_knowledge"

    @property
    def description(self) -> str:
        return "Searches verified knowledge, documents, and policies."

    @property
    def parameters_schema(self) -> dict:
        return {
            "type": "OBJECT",
            "properties": {
                "query": {"type": "STRING", "description": "The search query."}
            },
            "required": ["query"],
        }

    @property
    def prompt_instruction(self) -> str:
        return (
            "• KNOWLEDGE USAGE RULE (`search_knowledge`):\n"
            "  1. Call this tool when asked domain or factual questions.\n"
            "  2. Base your spoken response strictly on the retrieved context in 1-2 concise sentences."
        )

    async def execute(self, args: dict, context: ToolExecutionContext) -> ToolResult:
        query = args.get("query", "")
        # Execute RAG semantic retrieval
        docs = await retriever.retrieve(query, limit=2)
        if not docs:
            return ToolResult(status="no_results", message="No matching documents found.")

        combined_text = "\n---\n".join([f"[{d.title}]: {d.text}" for d in docs])
        return ToolResult(
            status="success",
            message=combined_text,
            jit_instruction="Summarize the answer clearly in 1 spoken sentence.",
        )

# Register with VoiceAgent
agent = VoiceAgent(config=VoiceConfig(api_key=os.environ["GEMINI_API_KEY"]))
agent.register_tool(KnowledgeTool())

docs.title: 7. High-Throughput Batch Ingestion
docs.text:
For high-volume document ingestion, GeminiEmbeddings provides an asynchronous batching method powered by Google Gemini's batchEmbedContents API:

embeddings = GeminiEmbeddings(
    api_key="your-gemini-key",
    model="gemini-embedding-001",
    dimension=768,  # Configurable dense vector dimension
)

# Batch embed 500 chunks with automatic chunking and 429 rate limit backoff
chunk_texts = [c.text for c in document_chunks]
vectors = await embeddings.embed_batch(chunk_texts, batch_size=20)

# Upsert directly into your store
await store.upsert(document_chunks, vectors)

docs.title: 8. Pluggable Query Normalization Hook
docs.text:
When working with domain-specific vocabularies, dialects, or multilingual queries (e.g. Hindi/Devanagari, Gujarati, medical codes), pass a query_normalizer function into RAGRetriever:

def my_query_normalizer(raw_query: str) -> str:
    # Enrich or transliterate raw input before embedding & keyword searching
    return transliterate_or_expand_synonyms(raw_query)

retriever = RAGRetriever(
    embedding_model=embeddings,
    vector_store=store,
    query_normalizer=my_query_normalizer,
    default_limit=3,
)

docs.title: 9. Store Lifecycle & Delta-Sync Operations
docs.text:
All BaseVectorStore adapters expose uniform management APIs for live diagnostics and incremental file synchronization:

# 1. Fetch collection point counts, status, and dimensions
stats = await store.get_stats()
# => {"status": "online", "points_count": 750, "vectors_count": 750, "vector_size": 768}

# 2. Delete granular points by ID (when specific chunks are updated)
deleted_count = await store.delete_points(["chunk_uuid_1", "chunk_uuid_2"])

# 3. Purge all vectors by metadata filter (e.g. when a source file is removed from disk)
await store.delete_by_filter({"source_file": "obsolete_guide.pdf"})

docs.title: WhatsApp Notifications & Messaging
docs.text: edgevoiceai provides an integrated WhatsApp messaging pipeline designed specifically for voice agents. It features: - Multi-Provider Support: Works with the official Meta Cloud API (Direct Text & Approved Templates) or Custom Gateway / Webhook URLs. - Phone Number Normalization: Cleans and adds country calling codes automatically (e.g. 9876543210 $\rightarrow$ 919876543210). - Strict 2-Turn Confirmation Protocol: The model must verbally confirm the recipient's phone number and receive explicit confirmation before dispatching. - Zero-Boilerplate Agent Hook: Passing whatsapp=WhatsAppConfig(...) into VoiceConfig automatically initializes and registers the tool with the agent.

docs.title: Option A: Official Meta WhatsApp Business Cloud API
docs.text:
To send messages directly via Meta's Graph API:

# In your .env file or deployment environment:
export WHATSAPP_TOKEN="EAAG..."                 # Meta Permanent System User Access Token
export WHATSAPP_PHONE_NUMBER_ID="10492837482"   # Meta Registered Phone Number ID (Sender ID)
export WHATSAPP_DEFAULT_TEMPLATE=""             # Leave empty for direct text, or name an approved template
export WHATSAPP_DEFAULT_LANGUAGE="en"           # Template language code (e.g. "en", "gu", "hi")
export WHATSAPP_PHONE_PREFIX="91"               # Default country calling code (e.g. 91 for India, 1 for US)

docs.title: Option B: Custom Gateway, Internal Proxy, or Webhook Relay
docs.text:
If your organization uses a custom microservice, SMS gateway, or webhook relay:

export WHATSAPP_SERVICE_URL="https://api.yourcompany.com/v1/whatsapp/send"
export WHATSAPP_API_KEY="your-gateway-secret-token"

The client sends a clean JSON payload to your custom URL: 

{
  "phone": "919876543210",
  "message": "Here is your agricultural health report...",
  "template": "",
  "language": "en"
}

docs.title: Automatic Agent Registration (Recommended)
docs.text:
Pass WhatsAppConfig directly into VoiceConfig. VoiceAgent automatically creates and registers WhatsAppNotificationTool into its tool registry:

import os
from edgevoiceai import VoiceAgent, VoiceConfig, WhatsAppConfig

# 1. Load config from environment
wa_config = WhatsAppConfig.from_env()

# 2. Attach to VoiceConfig
agent_config = VoiceConfig(
    api_key=os.environ["GEMINI_API_KEY"],
    whatsapp=wa_config,  # Auto-registers WhatsApp tool and rules
)

agent = VoiceAgent(config=agent_config)

docs.title: Explicit Tool Customization
docs.text:
You can also instantiate and customize the tool manually:

from edgevoiceai import WhatsAppConfig, WhatsAppNotificationTool

wa_config = WhatsAppConfig(
    token=os.environ.get("WHATSAPP_TOKEN", ""),
    phone_number_id=os.environ.get("WHATSAPP_PHONE_NUMBER_ID", ""),
    phone_prefix="91",
    timeout=15.0,
)

wa_tool = WhatsAppNotificationTool(config=wa_config)
agent.register_tool(wa_tool)

docs.title: 3. The Strict 2-Turn Confirmation Protocol
docs.text:
Outbound messaging must never be triggered prematurely on the first turn. If a user says "Send the formula to my WhatsApp on 9876543210", the assistant must not send it immediately.

sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor User as User (Voice)
    participant Agent as VoiceAgent (AI)
    participant Tool as WhatsAppNotificationTool
    participant Meta as Meta Cloud API

    User->>Agent: "Send this recipe to 9876543210 on WhatsApp"
    Note over Tool: Turn 1: Gate Closed
    Agent->>User: "Your phone number is 9876543210, correct?"
    User->>Agent: "Yes, that's right."
    Note over Tool: Turn 2: Gate Verified
    Agent->>Tool: execute(phone="9876543210", message="Recipe...")
    Tool->>Meta: POST /v21.0/{phone_number_id}/messages
    Meta-->>Tool: 200 OK {"messages": [{"id": "wamid.HBg..."}]}
    Tool-->>Agent: ToolResult(status="success")
    Agent->>User: "I've sent the recipe to your WhatsApp!"

docs.title: Runtime Verification Gate
docs.text:
If the model hallucinates and attempts to call send_whatsapp_message on the very first turn before obtaining verbal verification, WhatsAppNotificationTool intercepts the call and returns:

{
  "status": "pending_confirmation",
  "message": "PHONE CONFIRMATION REQUIRED: First ask the user verbally: 'Your phone number is [phone_number], correct?' and stop speaking. Do not send until the user confirms."
}

This ensures zero accidental messages and zero dummy phone numbers.

docs.title: VoiceAgent & Configuration Reference
docs.text: This section documents the core runtime orchestration engine VoiceAgent and the system configuration dataclasses (VoiceConfig, AudioConfig, RAGConfig, and WhatsAppConfig).

docs.title: edgevoiceai.config
docs.text: Configuration classes for Voice AI Framework. Defines parameters for audio streaming, model setup, VAD, edge devices, notifications, and RAG.

docs.title: VoiceConfig dataclass
docs.text:
Central configuration object for a VoiceAgent instance. Compatible with Raspberry Pi, Linux, macOS, and Windows.

Source code in edgevoiceai/config.py 
@dataclass
class VoiceConfig:
    """
    Central configuration object for a VoiceAgent instance.
    Compatible with Raspberry Pi, Linux, macOS, and Windows.
    """

@dataclass(slots=True)
class WhatsAppConfig:
    """
    Configuration options for WhatsApp messaging in the Voice AI Framework.
    Natively supports:
      1. Official Meta / Facebook WhatsApp Business Cloud API (token, phone_number_id)
      2. Custom REST gateways / webhook relays (service_url, api_key)
    """
    token: str = ""  # Official Meta WhatsApp Cloud API Access Token
    phone_number_id: str = ""  # Official Meta Phone Number ID (sender ID)
    business_account_id: str = ""  # Meta WABA / Business Account ID (optional)
    api_version: str = "v21.0"  # Meta Graph API version

    # Generic or custom gateway parameters
    api_key: str = ""  # API key for generic/custom gateway (or alias for token)
    service_url: str = ""  # Custom service URL (auto-generated if phone_number_id is provided)
    provider: str = "auto"  # "auto" | "meta" | "generic" | "webhook"

    # Messaging defaults
    default_template: str = ""
    default_language: str = "en"
    phone_prefix: str = "91"  # Default country calling code
    timeout: float = 15.0

    # Custom auth header overrides
    auth_header_name: str | None = None  # e.g., "Authorization" or "API-KEY"
    auth_header_prefix: str | None = None  # e.g., "Bearer "

    # Voice AI safety & guardrails
    require_two_turn_confirmation: bool = True

    # Localized / customized conversational messages
    invalid_phone_message: str | None = None
    confirmation_prompt_message: str | None = None
    success_message: str | None = None
    prompt_instruction: str | None = None


    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        # Standardize token and api_key aliases
        if not self.token and self.api_key:
            object.__setattr__(self, "token", self.api_key)
        elif not self.api_key and self.token:
            object.__setattr__(self, "api_key", self.token)

        # Resolve provider
        if self.provider == "auto":
            if self.phone_number_id:
                object.__setattr__(self, "provider", "meta")
            elif self.service_url:
                object.__setattr__(self, "provider", "generic")
            else:
                object.__setattr__(self, "provider", "generic")

        # Auto-construct Meta Graph API endpoint URL if phone_number_id is provided
        if self.provider == "meta" and self.phone_number_id:
            constructed_url = f"https://graph.facebook.com/{self.api_version}/{self.phone_number_id}/messages"
            object.__setattr__(self, "service_url", constructed_url)

class VoiceAgent:
    """
    Full-duplex real-time Conversational Voice AI Agent.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        config: VoiceConfig,
        tools: ToolRegistry | None = None,
        topic_guard: TopicGuard | None = None,
        farewell_detector: FarewellDetector | None = None,
        memory: BaseMemoryStore | None = None,
        entity_extractor: EntityExtractor | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        self.config = config
        self.tools = tools or ToolRegistry()
        self.topic_guard = topic_guard
        self.farewell_detector = farewell_detector or FarewellDetector()
        self.memory = memory
        self.entity_extractor = entity_extractor

        # Auto-register WhatsApp notification tool if configured
        if self.config.whatsapp is not None:
            wa_tool = WhatsAppNotificationTool(config=self.config.whatsapp)
            if not self.tools.has_tool(wa_tool.name):
                self.tools.register(wa_tool)

        # Optional event callbacks
        self.on_user_speech_start: Callable[[], None] | None = None
        self.on_ai_speech_start: Callable[[], None] | None = None
        self.on_turn_complete: Callable[[str], None] | None = None
        self.on_interrupted: Callable[[], None] | None = None
        self.on_tool_executed: Callable[[str, dict[str, Any], Any], None] | None = None

        self._shutdown_event = asyncio.Event()



    def register_tool(self, tool: BaseTool) -> VoiceAgent:
        """Fluent interface to register a tool with the agent."""
        self.tools.register(tool)
        return self

    def stop(self) -> None:
        """Signals the agent to stop its running loop."""
        self._shutdown_event.set()

    async def run_edge(self, session_id: str = "default") -> None:
        """
        Runs the full always-listening voice loop on edge hardware
        (Raspberry Pi, Mac, Windows, Linux laptop).
        """
        if websockets is None:
            raise RuntimeError("websockets is required. Install with: pip install websockets")

        # 1. Resolve Audio Hardware Devices
        in_dev = AudioDeviceManager.find_device_index(self.config.input_device, is_input=True)
        out_dev = AudioDeviceManager.find_device_index(self.config.output_device, is_input=False)

        print("\n" + "=" * 60)
        print("🎙️  [VOICE AGENT INITIALIZED]")
        print("=" * 60)
        print(f"  Model            : {self.config.model}")
        print(f"  Voice            : {self.config.voice}")
        print(f"  Mic Device       : {'Default' if in_dev is None else f'Index {in_dev}'}")
        print(f"  Speaker Device   : {'Default' if out_dev is None else f'Index {out_dev}'}")
        print(f"  Interrupt Thresh : {self.config.interrupt_rms_threshold}")
        print(f"  Noise Gate Thresh: {self.config.noise_gate_threshold}")
        print("=" * 60 + "\n")

        # 2. Audio Pipeline Setup
        vad_config = VADConfig(
            interrupt_rms_threshold=self.config.interrupt_rms_threshold,
            ai_interrupt_threshold=self.config.ai_interrupt_threshold,
            noise_gate_threshold=self.config.noise_gate_threshold,
            hang_frames=self.config.hang_frames,
            streak_trigger=self.config.vad_streak_trigger,
            pre_buffer_max_frames=self.config.pre_buffer_max_frames,
        )
        vad = VoiceActivityDetector(vad_config)

        # Share a single PyAudio instance across mic and speaker
        pa: Any = None
        if PYAUDIO_AVAILABLE and pyaudio is not None:
            try:
                pa = pyaudio.PyAudio()
            except Exception as pa_err:
                print(f"⚠️  [PyAudio Init Warning]: {pa_err}")

        mic_stream = MicrophoneStream(
            pa=pa,
            device_index=in_dev,
            capture_rate=self.config.mic_capture_rate,
            target_rate=self.config.gemini_input_rate,
        )

        player = AudioPlayer(
            pa=pa,
            device_index=out_dev,
            sample_rate=self.config.speaker_sample_rate,
        )

        media_player = MediaAudioPlayer(media_dir=self.config.media_directory)

        ws_url = GeminiLiveProtocol.get_ws_url(
            self.config.api_key,
            base_url=self.config.ws_base_url or "wss://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/ws/google.ai.generativelanguage.v1beta.GenerativeService.BidiGenerateContent",
        )

        is_reconnect = False

        try:
            while not self._shutdown_event.is_set():
                try:
                    print(f"🔗 Connecting to Gemini Live ({self.config.model})...")
                    async with websockets.connect(
                        ws_url,
                        open_timeout=self.config.open_timeout,
                        close_timeout=self.config.close_timeout,
                        ping_interval=self.config.ping_interval,
                        max_size=None,
                    ) as gemini_ws:
                        # Build dynamic system instruction (base prompt + user memory + tool rules)
                        sys_instruction = await self.build_effective_system_instruction(session_id=session_id)

                        # Send handshake setup message
                        tools_schema = self.tools.to_gemini_tools_payload()
                        setup_payload = GeminiLiveProtocol.build_setup_message(
                            model=self.config.model,
                            system_instruction=sys_instruction,
                            voice_name=self.config.voice,
                            tools_declarations=tools_schema,
                            is_reconnect=is_reconnect,
                        )
                        await gemini_ws.send(json.dumps(setup_payload))

                        # Await setup confirmation
                        raw_setup = await asyncio.wait_for(gemini_ws.recv(), timeout=15.0)
                        setup_str = raw_setup.decode("utf-8") if isinstance(raw_setup, (bytes, bytearray)) else str(raw_setup)
                        setup_data = json.loads(setup_str)
                        if "setupComplete" in setup_data:
                            print("✅ [Gemini Live Connected & Ready!]")
                        else:
                            print(f"⚠️  [Unexpected Setup Response]: {setup_str[:200]}")

                        # Drain any mic frames buffered during connection
                        while not mic_stream.queue.empty():
                            try:
                                mic_stream.queue.get_nowait()
                            except Exception:
                                break

                        # Proactive greeting: trigger so the assistant speaks immediately on startup
                        if not is_reconnect and self.config.greeting_message:
                            greet_payload = {
                                "clientContent": {
                                    "turns": [{"role": "user", "parts": [{"text": self.config.greeting_message}]}],
                                    "turnComplete": True,
                                }
                            }
                            await gemini_ws.send(json.dumps(greet_payload))
                            print("🎙️ [Greeting Triggered] — Assistant is introducing itself.")

                        # Session state
                        ai_is_speaking = False
                        tool_is_executing = False
                        interrupted_at = 0.0
                        user_has_spoken = not is_reconnect
                        session_turn = 0
                        user_speaking_logged = False

                        # ── Task A: Mic -> Gemini ──────────────────────────────
                        async def mic_to_gemini() -> None:
                            nonlocal ai_is_speaking, interrupted_at, user_has_spoken, user_speaking_logged
                            while not self._shutdown_event.is_set():
                                pcm = mic_stream.get_chunk(block=False)
                                if pcm is None:
                                    await asyncio.sleep(0.005)
                                    continue

                                if tool_is_executing:
                                    continue

                                rms = compute_rms(pcm)

                                # Check barge-in on media audio file
                                if media_player.is_playing():
                                    if vad.check_barge_in(pcm, self.config.interrupt_rms_threshold):
                                        print(f"\n⚡ [Interruption detected (RMS {int(rms)}) -> Stopping audio file]")
                                        media_player.stop()
                                        if self.on_interrupted:
                                            self.on_interrupted()
                                    continue

                                # Check barge-in on AI speech
                                if ai_is_speaking or player.is_playing():
                                    if vad.check_barge_in(pcm, self.config.ai_interrupt_threshold):
                                        print(f"\n⚡ [AI Interrupted (RMS {int(rms)}) -> Clearing speaker]")
                                        player.clear()
                                        media_player.stop()
                                        ai_is_speaking = False
                                        interrupted_at = time.time()
                                        user_has_spoken = True
                                        if self.on_interrupted:
                                            self.on_interrupted()
                                    else:
                                        continue

                                # Noise gate and speech streaming
                                should_stream, frames = vad.process_chunk(pcm)
                                if should_stream:
                                    if not user_speaking_logged and vad.gate_open:
                                        print(f"\n🎤 [Voice detected: RMS {int(rms)}]", flush=True)
                                        user_speaking_logged = True
                                    user_has_spoken = True
                                    for frame in frames:
                                        try:
                                            payload = GeminiLiveProtocol.encode_audio_chunk(frame)
                                            await gemini_ws.send(payload)
                                        except Exception:
                                            break
                                else:
                                    user_speaking_logged = False

                        # ── Task B: Gemini -> Speaker + Tools ──────────────────
                        async def gemini_to_speaker() -> None:
                            nonlocal ai_is_speaking, tool_is_executing, interrupted_at, session_turn
                            ai_text_parts: list[str] = []
                            pending_audio_url: str | None = None

                            async for raw_msg in gemini_ws:
                                if self._shutdown_event.is_set():
                                    break

                                msg_str = raw_msg.decode("utf-8") if isinstance(raw_msg, (bytes, bytearray)) else str(raw_msg)
                                parsed = GeminiLiveProtocol.parse_message(msg_str)
                                if parsed.error:
                                    print(f"⚠️  [Gemini Error]: {parsed.error}")
                                    continue

                                if parsed.interrupted:
                                    player.clear()
                                    ai_is_speaking = False
                                    interrupted_at = time.time()
                                    ai_text_parts.clear()
                                    continue

                                # Handle tool calls
                                if parsed.tool_calls:
                                    tool_is_executing = True
                                    try:
                                        ctx = ToolExecutionContext(
                                            session_id=session_id,
                                            current_turn=session_turn,
                                        )
                                        fn_responses: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
                                        for tc in parsed.tool_calls:
                                            fn_name = tc.get("name", "")
                                            fn_args = tc.get("args", {})
                                            call_id = tc.get("id", "")

                                            tool_res = await self.tools.dispatch(fn_name, fn_args, ctx)
                                            if tool_res.queued_audio_url:
                                                pending_audio_url = tool_res.queued_audio_url

                                            fn_responses.append({
                                                "response": {
                                                    "name": fn_name,
                                                    "content": tool_res.to_gemini_response_content(),
                                                },
                                                "id": call_id,
                                            })
                                            if self.on_tool_executed:
                                                self.on_tool_executed(fn_name, fn_args, tool_res)

                                        if fn_responses:
                                            tool_payload = GeminiLiveProtocol.encode_tool_responses(fn_responses)
                                            await gemini_ws.send(tool_payload)
                                    finally:
                                        tool_is_executing = False

                                # Process audio output
                                if parsed.audio_pcm_chunks:
                                    if interrupted_at > 0.0 and (time.time() - interrupted_at) < 0.8:
                                        continue
                                    if is_reconnect and not user_has_spoken:
                                        continue

                                    ai_is_speaking = True
                                    for chunk in parsed.audio_pcm_chunks:
                                        player.feed(chunk)

                                if parsed.text_parts:
                                    ai_text_parts.extend(parsed.text_parts)

                                if parsed.turn_complete:
                                    ai_is_speaking = False
                                    interrupted_at = 0.0
                                    full_text = "".join(ai_text_parts).strip()
                                    ai_text_parts.clear()
                                    session_turn += 1

                                    # Notify turn complete immediately
                                    if self.on_turn_complete and full_text:
                                        self.on_turn_complete(full_text)

                                    # Record turn in memory and schedule entity extraction in background
                                    if self.memory and full_text:
                                        await self.memory.add_message(
                                            session_id, role="assistant", content=full_text
                                        )
                                        if self.entity_extractor:
                                            asyncio.create_task(
                                                self.entity_extractor.extract_and_update(
                                                    session_id, self.memory
                                                )
                                            )

                                    # Only wait for speaker if an external pre-recorded audio file is queued
                                    if pending_audio_url:
                                        while player.is_playing() and not self._shutdown_event.is_set():
                                            await asyncio.sleep(0.04)
                                        media_player.play(pending_audio_url)
                                        pending_audio_url = None

                                    if self.farewell_detector.is_farewell(full_text):
                                        print("👋 [Session concluded by farewell]")
                                        self.stop()
                                        break

                        # Run both tasks concurrently
                        t_mic = asyncio.create_task(mic_to_gemini())
                        t_spk = asyncio.create_task(gemini_to_speaker())
                        done, pending = await asyncio.wait(
                            [t_mic, t_spk], return_when=asyncio.FIRST_COMPLETED
                        )
                        for task in pending:
                            task.cancel()
                            try:
                                await task
                            except (asyncio.CancelledError, Exception):
                                pass

                        for task in done:
